visual.general_description: Photograph-quality scan of a 12-lead ECG with rhythm strips.
visual.detailed_description: A 12-lead electrocardiogram printed on pink gridded paper. A calibration pulse mark is at the left of each row. The first three rows carry the lead labels I, aVR, V1, V4 (row 1), II, aVL, V2, V5 (row 2) and III, aVF, V3, V6 (row 3), with dashed vertical lines separating the four lead columns. Below them are three long continuous strips labelled II, V2 and V5. Narrow QRS complexes occur at widely separated, similar intervals across the strips, with small low-amplitude deflections between them. Two filled black dots sit at the bottom edge. No printed heart-rate value, paper speed, gain, date, time or name is visible.

visual.general_description: ECG scan with printed paper speed, gain and filter settings.
visual.detailed_description: A 12-lead electrocardiogram on pink gridded paper in a 3-by-4 layout with a long lead II strip at the bottom. Lead labels printed: I, aVR, V1, V4 (row 1), II, aVL, V2, V5 (row 2), III, aVF, V3, V6 (row 3) and II (bottom strip). The tracings show regularly spaced, broad complexes in leads II, III, aVF and V1 to V6, mostly with a downward initial deflection followed by an upright rounded wave, and a baseline that is noisy in leads I, aVL and III. Lead aVR shows smaller complexes. A footer line at the bottom prints device text, "Speed: 25 mm/sec", "Limb: 10 mm/mV", "Chest: 10.0 mm/mV", a boxed "F 50~ 0.15-150 Hz", "PH100B", "CL?" and "P?". A black rounded mark is at the lower left corner. Separate narrow pacing spikes could not be reliably resolved at this resolution.
